answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to one slow service record, like a mesa rising layer by layer: a job only counts once its client has checked the work, and the next job in that chain cannot start until that check lands, so one operator running many fake identities must wait through each chain in turn instead of spinning them up together. A pulse of random verification tasks stops idle identities from coasting, and the nectar of the system, the useful work itself, accrues only to chains that stay clean, so a hundredth fake identity costs a hundredth slow climb, not a bulk discount.
